SECTION: Chapter 6 CODE OF CONDUCT FOR LSPU STUDENTS (Definition and Type of Offenses) | Article 8. Mental Health Services/Treatment
Article 8. Mental Health Services/Treatment

A. University Psychological First Aid:

1. Assure the individual's safety and well-being

2. Identify and help those who are in need.

3. Re-establish social support

4. Return to school and familiar routines

5. Facilitate communication among families, students, and community agencies

6. Educate those affected by stressful and traumatic events about the expected psychological responses and essential coping tools.

7. Be aware of and take steps to meet the most basic practical requirements

8. Solicit people’s concerns and try to address them

9. Encourage participation in daily activities (if possible) and use positive coping mechanisms.

10. Use local support systems or trained clinicians to get the needed help, to the extent possible.

B. Other University Services

1. Variety of assistance programs where options with the school nurse or school counselor could be discussed.

2. Play therapy, relaxation therapy, biofeedback, and visualization are just some of the methods that can be used to help patients.

3. On-site consultations, classroom visits and homeroom observations can all be part of a regular consultation schedule.

Goals The following are the main goals of the LSPU Mental Health Services Unit: • Prevent, intervene and informed the school, families, and community about mental health services. • Ensure that the university population's psychiatric, neurologic, and psychosocial needs are met through a comprehensive university mental health care system. • Sustain provision of counseling services to the needy by the universitytrained school psychologists, guidance counselors, and school nurses. • Provide intensive programs and activities to improve the health and wellbeing of the academic community before it gets out of hand.

This includes not only the absence of mental illness, but also the promotion of social, emotional, and behavioral health in addition to a person's overall health.

Mental Health Services Workgroup University Health Risk Management Team The University Health Risk Management Team (UHRMT) is a vital support system that helps to prevent or reduce any danger on and off campus (HRMT). Team members have specific responsibilities for them to be effective.
develops, and implements Suicide Prevention Education for the school community in coordination with the SRMT, administrators, academic and support units, and outside organizations. • Coordinates with HRMT members and parents • Made available of the counseling and support services to students and their families • Monitors the individual's re-entry process • Debriefs students and staff in coordination with HRMT, administrators, academic and support units • Ensures ethical standards in the safekeeping and confidentiality of each individual records.

D. Medical Personnel • They will work with the university's guidance counselors and guidance faculty facilitators during the crisis to ensure that students' needs are met. • Assist with securing transportation to a hospital or clinic if medical attention is required • Make an appointment for the person with a specialist. • Monitor the re-entry processes of the individual

E. Communications Officer (in case of mental illness with suicidal attempt) • Secure the permission of the family or a legitimate source to announce the difficult situation publicly • Make public announcements about suicides that have occurred.

F.

trace.answer_for_eval:
The university offers the following mental health services:

1. University Psychological First Aid:
   - Assures safety and well-being
   - Identifies and helps those in need
   - Re-establishes social support
   - Facilitates return to school and routines
   - Facilitates communication among families, students, and community agencies
   - Educates affected individuals about psychological responses and coping tools
   - Meets basic practical needs
   - Addresses concerns
   - Encourages participation in daily activities and positive coping mechanisms
   - Uses local support systems or trained clinicians for help

2. Other University Services:
   - Assistance programs discussed with school nurse or counselor
   - Play therapy, relaxation therapy, biofeedback, visualization
   - On-site consultations, classroom visits, homeroom observations

3. Additional support through the University Health Risk Management Team:
   - Suicide prevention education
   - Coordination with families and outside organizations
   - Counseling and support services for students and families
   - Monitoring re-entry processes
   - Confidential record-keeping
   - Medical personnel support during crises
   - Communication management in cases of mental illness with suicidal attempts
